national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Kyrie Andrew Irving''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|aɪ|r|i}} {{respelling|KY|ree}}; {{langx|lkt|Ȟéla|italic=no}}, {{literal translation|Little Mountain}}; born March 23, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year|Rookie of the Year]] after being selected by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. A nine-time [[NBA All-Star|All-Star]] and three-time member of the [[All-NBA Team]], Irving won an [[NBA championship]] with the Cavaliers in 2016. Irving played one year of [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] before joining the Cavaliers in 2011. He won the [[NBA All-Star Game Kobe Bryant Most Valuable Player Award|Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) award for the [[2014 NBA All-Star Game|2014 All-Star Game]]. In the [[2016 NBA Finals]], Irving made the championship-winning [[three-point field goal|three-pointer]] to complete the Cavaliers' historic comeback over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. After another Finals appearance in 2017, Irving requested a trade and was dealt to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He played with the Celtics for two seasons, after which Irving signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] as a [[free agent]] in 2019. After four seasons with the Nets, he requested a trade and was dealt to the Dallas Mavericks in 2023, with whom Irving reached his fourth NBA Finals in [[2024 NBA Finals|2024]]. He has also played for the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]], with which Irving won gold at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]]. In February 2020, he was elected as one of the seven vice-presidents of the [[National Basketball Players Association]], replacing [[Pau Gasol]].{{Cite web |date=February 17, 2020 |title=Kyrie replaces Pau as a VP of players' union |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28724791/kyrie-irving-replaces-pau-gasol-vp-players-union |access-date=July 8, 2021 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=May 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515062835/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28724791/kyrie-irving-replaces-pau-gasol-vp-players-union |url-status=live}} Irving's decision not to get [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated for COVID-19]] led to him missing the majority of the [[2021–2022 NBA season]]. Throughout his career, Irving has promoted numerous [[conspiracy theories]]. Some of these conspiracies, including tweeting a link to the film ''[[Hebrews to Negroes: Wake Up Black America]]'' (2018), have been characterized as [[Antisemitism|antisemitic]]. For a time prior, Irving promoted a theory that [[Modern flat Earth beliefs|the Earth is flat]], which he later recanted.{{cite web|last=Blackburn|first=Pete|date=October 1, 2018|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/kyrie-irving-apologizes-for-saying-earth-is-flat-claims-he-was-into-conspiracies/|title=Kyrie Irving apologizes for saying Earth is flat, claims he was 'into conspiracies'|website=CBS Sports|access-date=May 17, 2023}} Irving has written, directed, and acted in a number of advertisements as "Uncle Drew", which became [[Uncle Drew|a feature film]] in 2018. He has starred as himself in ''[[Kickin' It]]'' (2012) and has done [[voice acting|voicework]] in ''[[We Bare Bears]]'' (2016) and ''[[Family Guy]]'' (2018). ==Early life== Irving was born in [[Melbourne]], Australia, on March 23, 1992;{{Cite web |last=Ryan |first=Conor |date=June 25, 2013 |title=Sharing talent on a big trip home |url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/leader/east/melbourneborn-nba-superstar-kyrie-irving-visiting-hometown-running-camps-at-state-basketball-centre-in-wantirna/news-story/2ee9f1086de613c314a10ff6abeae69a |access-date=July 8, 2021 |website=Herald Sun |archive-date=March 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220318044329/https://www.heraldsun.com.au/leader/east/melbourneborn-nba-superstar-kyrie-irving-visiting-hometown-running-camps-at-state-basketball-centre-in-wantirna/news-story/2ee9f1086de613c314a10ff6abeae69a |url-status=live}} the son of [[Drederick Irving]] and Elizabeth (née Larson) Irving, American expatriates.{{Cite web |last=Boyer |first=Mary Schmitt |date=June 26, 2011 |title=For Kyrie and Dred Irving, a long, winding road took them to a magical draft night (and the Cleveland Cavaliers) |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2011/06/for_kyrie_and_dred_irving_a_lo.html |access-date=July 29, 2021 |website=The Plain Dealer |archive-date=July 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729203600/https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2011/06/for_kyrie_and_dred_irving_a_lo.html |url-status=live}} He has an older sister, Asia, and a younger half-sister, London. [[File:Kyrie Irving (8467319877).jpg|thumb|Irving at the Greater Cleveland Sports Awards in January 2013]] ====2013–2014: All-Star Game MVP==== [[File:Kyrie Irving (10355742694).jpg|thumb|Irving in October 2013|left]] Fans chose Irving to be the starting point guard for the Eastern Conference in the 2014 NBA All-Star game.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/01/23/nba-all-star-2014-starters-announced-release/ |title=Curry starts in first All-Star Game; LeBron top vote-getter |first=Official |last=release |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=February 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140127013641/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/01/23/nba-all-star-2014-starters-announced-release |archive-date=January 27, 2014 |url-status=dead}} He was the All-Star game MVP, recording 31 points and 14 assists as the East beat the West 163–155.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140216/ESTWST/gameinfo.html |title=East at West |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=February 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207221846/http://www.nba.com/games/20140216/ESTWST/gameinfo.html |archive-date=February 7, 2015 |url-status=dead}} On February 28, 2014, Irving recorded his first career triple-double with 21 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds in a 99–79 victory over the Utah Jazz. |last=NBA |date=April 5, 2014 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} He averaged 20.8 points, 6.1 assists, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.5 steals on the season. ====2014–2015: Big Three formation and first NBA Finals==== [[File:20141017 Cleveland Cavaliers vs Dallas Mavericks.jpg|thumb|Irving shoots a [[jump shot (basketball)|jump shot]] vs the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in 2014]] On July 10, 2014, Irving signed a five-year, $90 million contract extension with the Cavaliers.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-sign-kyrie-irving-contract-extension |title=Cavaliers and Kyrie Irving Sign Contract Extension |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=July 11, 2014 |archive-date=July 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712232159/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-sign-kyrie-irving-contract-extension |url-status=live}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11200009/cleveland-cavaliers-announce-kyrie-irving-contract-extension |title=Cavs owner on Irving deal: Big piece of plan |date=July 10, 2014 |access-date=July 11, 2014 |archive-date=June 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623235822/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/11200009/cleveland-cavaliers-announce-kyrie-irving-contract-extension |url-status=live}} His contract extension came in the wake of [[LeBron James]]'s return to Cleveland and [[Kevin Love]]'s trade request from Minnesota, as the trio teamed up to start a new "Big Three" in Cleveland. After a shaky start to the season, where they fell to a 5–7 record after a November 22 loss to Toronto, the Cavaliers went on an eight-game winning streak, where Irving averaged 19.3 points per game, including a 37-point game against the New York Knicks on December 4.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/i/irvinky01/gamelog/2015/ |title=Kyrie Irving 2014-15 Game Log - Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=December 2, 2017 |archive-date=May 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525185228/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/i/irvinky01/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live}} After their streak-ending loss on December 11 to Oklahoma City, the Cavaliers went on to win just five more games in December, finishing 2014 at 18–14. All of the new Big Three missed time during December, contributing to the team's inconsistency and mediocre play. The Cavaliers began their 2015 schedule on January 2 as they snapped a three-game losing streak with Irving's help.
